meta.title: Act 1 — Land: Embervale
meta.what-tamed-counts: A `tamed` trigger's `species` names the WILD INSTANCE — `wild-sproutle`, never `sproutle` — because the fact carries the enemy that was bonded, not the companion it became (issue #178). That is the whole of how The First Bond refuses the penned practice animal: `penned-sproutle` is simply not in its list, a fact about the animal rather than about which quest was active.
meta.note: The six main quests of Act 1 (game-story.md §4, issue #143). Ordering is `prerequisites` and nothing else: `arc` is a journal heading, array order means nothing, and no counter anywhere says which act the player is in — the act boundary is the flags `sea-revealed` and `act-1-complete` that the last quest sets.
meta.what-freeing-is: `quest:land/the-red-thread` frees the penned Sproutle by killing what HOLDS it — `enemy:thread-anchor`, the knot the thread is wound onto — and not by bonding the animal itself. Bonding was the first shape of it and it is the wrong one: the animal is the thing you are freeing, so it must not also be the thing you interact with — and since issue #110 a second Sproutle is a real bond, so a player who bonded the penned one would have bought a companion, not freed anything. The `zone` on the trigger is what separates this from a Gloopling put down on the drove road.
meta.placeholder-model: `enemy:thread-anchor` wears its own builder — a knot of red cord wound over an angular shard, half-sunk, with a matching no-gait behaviour branch in combat/enemies.ts (issue #202). The variants stay one red at three exposures: it is one object somebody left in a cellar, not a wild population.
meta.the-act-seam: `quest:land/the-bellwether` closes the act, and it says so in two vocabularies on purpose. `quest:sea/salt-and-rope` will name it in `prerequisites`; everything else — dialogue, shops, the coast gateway — tests the flag `sea-revealed`. Nothing gates on `act-1-complete`: that one is a record, not a key. Both are set here and neither is ever cleared.
meta.the-arena-outlives-the-boss: The drove ground the Bellwether is fought on is not a prop of this quest. Act 4 stages `enemy:guardian/land` on the same ground (game-story.md §4), so the fight is a SPAWN on open country outside Stonewatch and nothing about the terrain, the town or the roads knows a boss is standing there. Kill it and the ground is what it was.
meta.what-put-down-counts: `quest:land/the-mill-road` counts ANY beast put down on the road — its `enemy-killed` trigger carries no `enemies` list, which is the trigger vocabulary for "any" (every filter is any when absent). A wild Sproutle counts the same as a Gloopling: the road is not safe and the quest is about walking it, not about which animals deserve it. An objective without the filter marks every enemy the world has up, because every one of them is what it is counting.
meta.towns-stay-in-core: Act 1 adds no towns. `town:encampment`, `town:redbriar` and `town:stonewatch` ship in core and are referenced from here — the road planner routes one trunk and two spurs, so those three are the ground settlements the world has (game-story.md §1 rule 4).

data._behaviour: A BOSS BORROWS MANNERS. Its model is its own, and an animator poses parts by name, so the shape has to carry the parts the behaviour reaches for — body, head and four legs. The Snortle's charge is what a herd animal leading a stampede does, which is why it is that one and not the Peckit's dive.

data._variants: THREE OF ONE THING. The variant is picked by the height a spawn lands at (`variantForHeight`), and the list needs three — but this is not a wild population with a snow form and a desert form, it is one object somebody left in a cellar. So the three are the same red at three exposures, and it reads identically wherever the hold puts it.

objectives._no-trigger: HEARING HER OUT IS THE DIALOGUE, not an arrival: the warden's own offer row advances this, the way `talk-to-gain` works in quest 1. A town-arrival cannot do it — you are standing in Stonewatch when she offers it, and the arrival fired before the quest existed.
